blocks.heading: Designing a consistent recruitment pack
blocks.text: Recruitment documents should describe the same vacancy consistently. A job description states the role’s duties and responsibilities; a job specification states the relevant abilities, qualifications or experience required from the person. An application form gathers comparable evidence against those criteria. An advertisement attracts suitable applicants by stating the role, location, key requirements and how and when to apply. Avoid vague requests for a wonderful person or irrelevant conditions that do not help perform the job. Distinguish essential criteria from desirable experience so useful applicants are not excluded by an unnecessarily high barrier. The documents should support a fair evidence-based comparison, not guarantee that the selected person will perform perfectly.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Nela Repairs in Tsumeb needs a full-time bookings assistant to record customer requests, maintain the repair diary, confirm collection times and communicate changes. The assistant reports to the office supervisor. Work requires accurate records, clear English communication and basic computer skills; previous booking experience is desirable, not essential. Initial system instruction will be provided. Original pack: Job description—Bookings assistant, Nela Repairs, Tsumeb; reports to office supervisor; record requests, update diary, confirm collections and communicate changes; full-time stated hours supplied at application. Specification—essential accurate record keeping, clear English communication and basic computer use; desirable booking experience. Application fields—name, contact, relevant skills and examples, relevant work history, availability and referee details with permission. Advertisement—Nela Repairs seeks a full-time bookings assistant in Tsumeb; duties and essential skills as above; previous booking experience desirable; system instruction provided; obtain the form at the fictional Nela Repairs workshop office, 18 Oryx Lane, Tsumeb, and return it by 31 October 2026. The pack connects criteria to the actual tasks.

blocks.heading: Job descriptions
blocks.text: A job description is a document which outlines the responsibilities and duties expected to be carried out by someone employed to do a specific job. Include the title, reporting relationship, purpose and relevant main duties. It describes the job rather than listing the person’s qualifications. A concise description supports both recruitment and later understanding of responsibilities.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Nela Repairs in Tsumeb needs a full-time bookings assistant to record customer requests, maintain the repair diary, confirm collection times and communicate changes. The assistant reports to the office supervisor. Work requires accurate records, clear English communication and basic computer skills; previous booking experience is desirable, not essential. Initial system instruction will be provided. Original job description: Title—Bookings assistant. Employer/location—Nela Repairs, Tsumeb. Reports to—Office supervisor. Purpose—Maintain accurate repair bookings and customer arrangements. Duties—Record requests; update the diary; confirm collection times; notify the supervisor and customer of changes; protect the accuracy of records. Working arrangement—Full-time, Monday to Friday, 08:00–17:00 with the agreed break. Each duty follows the stated vacancy rather than inventing technical repair responsibilities.

blocks.heading: Job specifications
blocks.text: A job specification is a document which outlines the requirements, qualifications and expertise required from a person to do a specific job. Connect each criterion to the work and distinguish essential from desirable criteria. It describes the person needed, not the tasks alone. Unnecessary requirements can exclude capable applicants and shrink the pool without improving performance.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Nela Repairs seeks a Tsumeb bookings assistant for accurate diary entries and clear customer confirmations. Basic computer use is essential. Previous booking experience is useful but can be learned after appointment. Choose job-related essential and desirable person criteria. Original specification: Essential—accurate record keeping demonstrated by an example or practical task; clear English communication for customer confirmations; basic computer skills for the diary; ability to organise overlapping requests. Desirable—previous booking or customer-record experience. System-specific experience is not essential because initial instruction is provided. Do not demand a technical repair qualification for this administrative role.

blocks.heading: Application forms
blocks.text: An application form gathers comparable information from applicants so the employer can assess relevant criteria consistently. Use clearly labelled spaces for contact information, relevant skills, experience and availability. Ask for evidence, not just a yes/no claim of being suitable. Keep the form focused on the job and explain submission. It does not replace an interview or practical assessment where those are needed.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Nela Repairs in Tsumeb needs a full-time bookings assistant to record customer requests, maintain the repair diary, confirm collection times and communicate changes. The assistant reports to the office supervisor. Work requires accurate records, clear English communication and basic computer skills; previous booking experience is desirable, not essential. Initial system instruction will be provided. Original application form: Vacancy—Bookings assistant, Nela Repairs. Name: ____ Contact details: ____ Relevant record-keeping experience or example: ____ Computer skills and example of use: ____ Example of clear customer communication: ____ Relevant work history: ____ Availability for the stated hours/start: ____ Referee and contact, with permission: ____ Applicant confirmation that information is accurate: ____ Date: ____. These fields gather evidence aligned to the specification.

blocks.heading: Job advertisements
blocks.text: A job advertisement communicates a vacancy to attract suitable applicants. State the employer, title, location, main duties, key essential criteria, relevant working arrangement, application method and a clear closing date. It should be accurate and consistent with the description and specification. Too little detail creates unsuitable applications; unnecessary demands can discourage suitable people. Choose a channel applicants can access.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work

Full-time role recording repair requests, maintaining the diary and confirming customer collections. Essential: accurate records, clear English communication and basic computer skills. blocks.heading: Worked practice: Recruitment materials and training suitability
blocks.text:
Fictional Tula Goods appoints a new clerk to use its simple stock system. A competent colleague is available, and errors can be contained in practice records before live use. It compares supervised on-the-job learning with an external course on a different system. For part (b) only, no competent workplace trainer is now available, while a specialist external course on Tula’s actual system is available. Other facts remain unchanged.

a Evaluate Tula’s options under the original facts. [12]
b Evaluate them after the trainer and course facts change. Explain whether the recommendation changes. [12]

a Prefer the available competent workplace guidance using practice records, since it fits the task and controls errors. The external course’s different system weakens transfer, though its structure could be helpful. Plan instruction, practice, feedback and assessment rather than assume observation is enough. b Without a competent colleague, informal workplace learning risks mistakes or poor habits. The specialist course now covers Tula’s actual system, removing the original mismatch. Prefer the relevant off-the-job course if time and cost are manageable, then reinforce it through supervised practice and checks on return. The choice changes with expertise and relevance, not because one method is universally best.
